chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a hunting dog that was released but its owner did not send it (intentionally), so it hunted; then the owner caught up with it and it had already killed the prey. Should he eat from it? He said: 'No.' And he said: 'If it hunts and the owner has named (God), let him eat; and if it hunts and the owner did not name, let him not eat. And this is from "What you have taught of the hunting beasts, making them hunt".'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from a hunting dog if the owner did not explicitly send it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the condition of *tasmiyah* (reciting God's name) for game caught by hunting dogs, distinguishing between intentional release and accidental hunting. The ruling hinges on whether the owner explicitly named God when sending the dog, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the ritual sanctity of consumption. This interpretation aligns with the Quranic verse 5:4, which permits eating what hunting beasts catch provided God's name is mentioned upon sending them.
